title: Whole service is one home laptop
evidence: Power cut, ISP outage, lid close/sleep, macOS update restart, theft or a dead battery take every user's scans down at once. It already ran flat on 2026-11-18. No spare, no failover.
fix: Move the server to a small paid cloud host (or at minimum a second box) with a restart policy
fix_cost: about $10-40/month plus a day or two to move
dup_of: gap 93, R03, R04, R07, starting point 6

title: Memory exhaustion on the 8 GB box
evidence: 85 MB free, swap in use, load test broke at 16 non-stop users. Server peaks near 2 GB while five Claude sessions, Chrome, Spotify and jobs share the machine. An OOM kill during a weekend peak drops everyone.
fix: Dedicate the machine or move the server; remove non-server workloads

title: Unsandboxed AI sessions share an account with user data and keys
evidence: Two Claude sessions run with permission checks off and can drive Chrome, one is steerable from a phone, all as the one macOS user that owns the shopper database, API keys and tunnel credentials. One prompt-injected web page or a lost phone gives an attacker the data and the Apple/GitHub/Cloudflare sessions in that Chrome.
fix: Separate OS user (or machine) for the server; AI sessions never on the host holding user data or logged-in accounts

title: FileVault off on the machine holding user data
evidence: Theft or a repair shop gives full read of device IDs, scan history, location-derived data and secrets. In Quebec a confidentiality incident must be recorded and may need reporting to the regulator.
fix: Enable FileVault (and keep server on a headless auto-login plan) or move host
fix_cost: minutes, but forces re-plan of auto-restart

title: Backups only on the same laptop
evidence: Disk failure, theft, fire or ransomware loses the shopper data and purchase mapping with the backup. Restores probably never rehearsed.
fix: Nightly encrypted copy off-site (cloud bucket), plus one tested restore

title: Server survives reboot unattended?
evidence: Spotify is used as a wake alarm, so the Mac sleeps. After a power cut or forced update restart, the tunnel and server only return if launchd starts them at boot with no login and sleep is disabled. Not stated.
fix: launchd services, auto power-on after outage, sleep disabled, a reboot drill

title: App hard-wired to one domain, no kill switch or failover
evidence: If relay.anjiawenda.com lapses, the registrar or Cloudflare account is compromised or suspended, every installed copy dies until a new App Review passes. Domain paid only to 2027-08-19; a hijack lets an attacker answer as the server.
fix: Auto-renew multi-year, 2FA and recovery on registrar and Cloudflare, remote-config fallback host in the app
fix_cost: small, but the app change needs a release

title: Auto-deploy on push is a remote-code path to the laptop
evidence: Anyone or any tool able to push to main (stolen token, AI session, bad dependency) runs code on the machine with user data after tests pass. Tests-only gate; no rollback, no staging, deploy every 30 s can restart mid-request.
fix: Protected branch, 2FA, signed or reviewed deploys, health-checked rollback

title: Old app versions break when server deploys change the API
evidence: App Review takes days and users do not update. Server auto-deploys every push, so any breaking response change strands installed apps with no quick fix.
fix: API versioning, minimum-version gate, additive changes only

title: Outage detection is slow and goes to one inbox
evidence: GitHub Actions cron probes every 30 minutes (often delayed; schedules are disabled after 60 days of repo inactivity) and emails Jamin only. A night or exam outage lasts hours unnoticed.
fix: External uptime monitor at 1 minute with phone push

title: One operator, one support inbox
evidence: 10,000 users produce hundreds of tickets, refund questions and review replies. Single person, student, full-time internship from May 2027. Unanswered support and outages become one-star reviews that kill ranking.
fix: Canned replies, FAQ in app, ticket tool, defined hours, helper (Aurik)
fix_cost: a few hours plus ongoing time
dup_of: starting point 4, R05, R06, R18, R22

title: App Review guideline 4.2 (web app in a wrapper)
evidence: Not on any list (no hit for guideline 4.2 or minimum functionality in the four files). Checked: native/package.json carries @capacitor-mlkit/barcode-scanning, text-recognition, camera, haptics, and the UI is bundled in the app (native/www), so it is a native camera scanner and not a bare website view. Risk is low; the reviewer-notes line that says so is the only addition worth making. Original reasoning: Apple rejects apps that are essentially a repackaged website. Camera scan, native features and offline value must be evident, with notes for the reviewer.
fix: Use native camera/barcode, haptics, share, notifications as appropriate; write reviewer notes
fix_cost: days if native features are thin

title: Reviewer sees an empty app
evidence: Checked docs/store/listing.md section App Review notes: it already gives a demo scan, typed search with an example and an attached barcode image (UPC 055773000795), so a reviewer outside Canada is covered. Only open: that the barcode image is actually attached on submit. Original reasoning: Apple reviewers are not in Canadian shops; scanning a US or random product returns no answer (only 44% get any answer even in real use). Looks like a broken app: guideline 2.1 rejection.
fix: A demo product set, reviewer notes with barcodes that work, sensible empty state

title: Purchases never proven
evidence: 0 purchases; scan limit is off until a test purchase works. Apple requires working IAP, restore purchases, subscription terms and privacy/EULA links on the paywall, and a paywall the reviewer can reach. A broken first purchase flow loses the only revenue.
fix: Sandbox and TestFlight purchase, restore, expiry and refund path end to end

title: Core promise fails most of the time
evidence: 44% of scans get any answer, about 25% a shop price. Three of four scans disappoint; day-1 retention and ratings suffer before growth starts. 10,000 users needs a far higher hit rate or a clear fallback value.
fix: Raise coverage on the most-scanned products, fix the no-answer screen to still give value

title: Stale or wrong price labelled as good deal
evidence: Weekly price file, shop and postcode price variation, and a model-guessed range can all produce a confident wrong verdict. Misleading price claims create trust loss and potential consumer-protection exposure.
fix: Show source and age of each price, label estimates clearly, never present a model range as a shop price

title: Open endpoints invite scripted abuse and cost burn
evidence: App talks to one public address; unless the server verifies the app (App Attest) and rate-limits per device, anyone can script it to drain the Claude ask cap (10,000/month), Open Food Facts quota and CPU. Cloudflare free offers little bot protection.
fix: Per-device and per-IP limits, App Attest or signed requests, cap-hit degrade path
dup_of: R41, A3, A7 (adds: App Attest named as the real fix in app/src/rate-limit.ts line 205 but not built)

title: Self-asserted device identity and entitlements
evidence: If the server trusts a device-supplied ID or entitlement flag, users can forge Plus or read others' history. Entitlement must come from RevenueCat server-side, with webhooks and cached grace if RevenueCat or the server is down.
fix: Server-verified entitlement, random unguessable IDs, cached entitlement in app

title: Open Food Facts at 12 a minute caps growth
evidence: 12/min is about 17,000 lookups a day total. New products from thousands of users queue behind it; users wait or get nothing.
fix: Cache aggressively, pre-load the popular products from the OFF dump, queue with user feedback
dup_of: R35 (adds the arithmetic, checked: app/src/open-food-facts.ts spaces calls 5 s apart = 12 a minute for the whole server; a lookup that would wait more than 5 s becomes a miss, so two shoppers scanning new barcodes in the same 5 s lose one)

title: Public Overpass service as a runtime dependency
evidence: Shared public instance throttles and blocks heavy clients and sends users' coordinates to a third party. At scale shop lookups fail or the IP is banned.
fix: Cache by grid cell, precompute shops for Canada, round coordinates before sending
dup_of: R77 (the coordinate part is already handled: app/src/stores.ts snaps to a 0.01 degree grid, about 1.1 km)

title: Single-process Node plus SQLite limits writes
evidence: One event loop, one writer lock. Scan and usage-event writes from thousands of users, a weekly price import and a 4 GB catalogue in the same box contend; the import job can starve the live server.
fix: WAL mode, batch writes, run imports off-peak or elsewhere, load test at realistic rates

title: Quebec Law 25 duties
evidence: Named person responsible for personal data with published contact, plain-language policy, consent for location, assessment before sending data outside Quebec (Anthropic, RevenueCat, Cloudflare in the US), incident register, access and deletion requests. Penalties up to C$25M or 4% of turnover.
fix: Privacy officer line, policy update, vendor list, incident register, request process
dup_of: R47, R51, R63, gap 82 (person responsible already named in docs/store/privacy-fr.html line 31)

title: Quebec French language rules
evidence: Consumer contracts, paywall, terms and app in Quebec must be available in French (Charter of the French Language, Bill 96); French version precedes acceptance of the English one. Store listing too. Aurik handles French text but no agreement yet.
fix: Full French UI, French terms and privacy, French store listing, professional review

title: Partner agreement missing
evidence: No agreement with Aurik covering ownership of code, text and screens, revenue share, who holds the Apple account, exit. Disputes after revenue starts are expensive and can block the app.
fix: Short written agreement before launch

title: Personal liability and employer claims
evidence: Sole proprietor with Apple account in a personal name means personal liability for breaches or refunds, no insurance, and legal name and address shown on the store. An internship contract may carry moonlighting or IP-assignment clauses that touch the app.
fix: Consider incorporation, business insurance, read the intern contract IP clause with a lawyer before May
dup_of: gap 79, R54, legal review q19 and q26 (adds: business insurance is not mentioned in any of the four files; grep found nothing)

title: Apple privacy label and manifest must match reality
evidence: Camera, location, device IDs, usage events and third parties (Anthropic, RevenueCat) all require accurate privacy nutrition labels and a privacy manifest. A mismatch gets rejection or later removal.
fix: Audit data flows against the label before submission

title: Model price guess shown as fact
evidence: Already handled in code: app/public/js/lib/catalogue-range.js line 125 labels the Claude range "Estimated by AI", and verdict-chart.js carries a claude_estimate note. Not on any list because it is not a gap. Original reasoning: Haiku gives a 'typical range' when data is missing. Language models invent plausible numbers; presented without a clear estimate label it is a false price claim.
fix: Mark as AI estimate, show range not point, lower confidence wording

title: No acquisition path to 10,000
evidence: Not on any list: grep of the four files finds R75 (competitor copies) and R88 (Apple featuring) but no plan for reaching 10,000. The rating-prompt part is already safe: app/public/js/review-prompt.js asks only after a third good-verdict win, never after a miss, 120 days apart. Only the acquisition channel is missing. Original reasoning: 19 phones in 14 days. Grocery price apps (Flipp and similar) are well known. No store listing optimisation, no referral loop, no content channel stated; early one-star reviews from failed scans cap ranking.
fix: Pick one channel (TikTok/Reddit/Facebook groups for Canadian grocery savings), referral share card, ask for ratings only after a success

title: Apple small business program and refunds
evidence: Without enrolling in the Small Business Program Apple keeps 30% instead of 15%. Refunds come out of payouts. Payouts in USD or CAD need tax and banking set up; Jamin reports the income personally.
fix: Enroll, set up tax forms and banking, note income for tax

title: Anthropic spend and key exposure
evidence: Key in server environment readable by every session on the box; a leak or abuse burns credits; credit exhaustion breaks the estimate feature silently.
fix: Hard spend limit in the Anthropic console, key rotated, alert at 50% of budget

title: No staging and unsafe schema changes on live data
evidence: Auto-deploy with tests only; a migration that fails halfway on the shopper database has no pre-migration snapshot or rollback.
fix: Snapshot before migration, a staging copy, reversible migrations

title: No crash or error telemetry in the app
evidence: Unknown whether failed scans, camera errors or freezes are visible to the operator beyond server logs. Cannot find why 56% of scans give nothing without scan-level reasons.
fix: Log failure reason per scan, use Apple crash reports

title: Data retention and deletion
evidence: Scans and usage events grow without limit on a small disk; there is no stated retention period or user deletion path, which Law 25, PIPEDA and Apple may expect.
fix: Retention schedule, delete-my-data in app

title: Policy pages depend on a personal GitHub account
evidence: Apple requires live privacy and support URLs. A GitHub suspension or repo rename breaks them and can pull the app.
fix: Host on the product's own domain

title: Name and brand clearance
evidence: No mention of trademark search for Pexi or checking App Store name conflicts; a later forced rename after 10,000 installs is costly.
fix: CIPO and App Store name search before launch

title: Home ISP terms, hardware wear
evidence: Residential plans may restrict commercial hosting; a fanless Air held at load and plugged in constantly throttles and wears the battery.
fix: Cloud host removes both
